name: Renaissance banquet
region: Papal Rome, Venice and the courts of Italy and France
summary: The feast of the Italian court as Bartolomeo Scappi set it down in 1570. A kitchen of many cooks sends out many dishes at once: pies, roasts, candied fruit and sculpture in sugar. The cook uses the fork, the sugar and the spit with great skill.

philosophy.core_thesis: Show the power of the host with the number, the skill and the beauty of the dishes, and let sugar and pastry take the shape of buildings and beasts.
design_principles: Set three or four services of up to 30 dishes each, and set them in a pattern on the table.
Use sugar in the savoury dish and in the sculpture: marzipan, comfits and candied peel.
Bake game and meat in a pastry case, and decorate the case with a pattern of dough.
Roast on the spit with a sauce of citrus juice, and dress a roast bird in its own feathers.
Carve the roast at the table; a carver trained in the art cuts each bird.
Lay a fork, a knife and a spoon at the place of each guest, and a clean napkin.
Keep a clean and ordered kitchen: Scappi draws every tool and every station.
anti_patterns: A sauce thickened only with bread and heavy spice
A single course on a bare table
Chilli, potato or maize in a banquet dish
A sauce of roux and butter in the French style of 1651
A dish served by hand with no fork

plating.composition: A large platter holds a roast or a pie at its centre, with garnish of citrus, comfits or gilt leaf around it.
plating.plate: A silver or majolica platter for the dish and a pewter or silver plate for each guest.
plating.portion: Each guest takes a piece of 100 to 160 g and a spoon of sauce from a dish of 20 or more.
plating.height: A pie or a sugar piece stands 150 to 400 mm high; a roast bird lies low on its platter.
rules: Set each service as a pattern of dishes that mirrors across the table.
Gild a pie or a sugar piece with gold leaf for the high table.
Put a sculpture of sugar at the centre of the table for the dessert service.
Serve the fruit and the sweet comfits at the end, with the cheese.
Give each guest a fork and a knife, and wipe the rim of each dish.

pantry.rule: Use sugar, citrus and warm spice with game and veal, and let sugar close the meal.

technique.bases: A veal or capon broth, a pastry dough of flour, butter and egg, a boiled sugar syrup and an almond paste.
technique.details: A larded roast, a pie lid with a pattern of dough, a jelly poured round a cold dish, a fruit candied in syrup, a bird on the spit dressed in feathers.

flavour.profile: Sweet, sour and warm: sugar and cinnamon with lemon and orange juice, with roast meat and rich pastry.
flavour.balance: Citrus juice and vinegar lift the sweet sugar and the rich fat; spice is lighter than in the medieval feast.
flavour.fat: Butter, lard and olive oil give 30 to 45 per cent of the energy of a main dish.
flavour.seasoning: Salt, pepper, cinnamon and sugar, with a squeeze of lemon or bitter orange on a roast.

palette.strategy: Use the white of sugar and linen, the gold of pastry and gilt, and the deep red of wine and silver, in a hall lit by many candles.

service.format: Service in removes: many dishes at once in each of three or four services, with a cold service, a hot service and a service of fruit and sugar.
service.courses: Three to four services of 10 to 30 dishes, and at a great feast Scappi lists menus of over 100 dishes.
service.tableware: A silver or majolica platter, a pewter plate, a fork, a knife, a spoon, a glass and a linen napkin.
service.setting: A palace hall or a villa in Rome, with a long table under a canopy, musicians and a carver in the middle.

dishes.dish: Pasticcio of game in a pastry case
Pheasant on the spit, dressed in its feathers
Larded veal on the spit with orange juice
Sugar sculpture of a castle with marzipan figures

positive: fork and knife at the place
linen napkin folded in a shape
overhead view of a feast table

emotion.target_response: Delight and wonder at abundance: a table that is a stage, with the pleasure of skill, sugar and show.

use_cases: a menu for a historical dinner of the 16th century
a still life of a banquet table
avoid_when: the brief wants a New World food
the brief wants one plate per guest
the brief wants a lean, plain dish

modifiers.request: less sugar, more sauce and herbs
modifiers.how: Drop the sugar from the roast, cut the spice, add fines herbes and make the sauce with a roux and a stock.

modifiers.request: darker, with heavy spice and bread sauce
modifiers.how: Remove the fork, bring back the bread trencher and thicken each sauce with soaked bread and spice.

sources.title: Terence Scully (tr.), The Opera of Bartolomeo Scappi (2008)
